text: The applicant was born in 1957.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant lives in Yekaterinburg.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 18 March 2003, the applicant, Mr Sh., and Ms M. sent a notice to the head of Yekaterinburg town administration of their intention to stage a picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The picket was planned to take place between 25 and 28 March 2003 between 9 and 11 a.m.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The declared purpose of the picket was 'to attract public attention to violations of the human right of access to a court'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 19 March 2003, the head of the Committee for Public Relations and Mass Media of the Yekaterinburg town administration acknowledged receipt of the picket notice.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The head of the Committee for Public Relations and Mass Media of the Yekaterinburg town administration noted that, should the picket cause any inconvenience, such as blocking access to the court-house or impairing its normal functioning, the administration would have to intervene.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 20 March 2003, the head of the Yekaterinburg public security police ordered that the police should maintain public order and traffic safety during the picket.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 25 March 2003, the applicant and others held the picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: During the picket on 25 March 2003, the applicant and others distributed press clippings and leaflets about Mr Ovcharuk, the President of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court, who had allegedly been involved in corruption scandals.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: During the picket on 25 March 2003, the applicant and others collected signatures for the dismissal of Mr Ovcharuk, the President of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev, the first deputy president of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court, sent a letter to the head of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department of Yekaterinburg.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that, with the consent of the Yekaterinburg town administration, a group of citizens comprising Mr Sh., Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), and Ms M. held a picket in front of the building of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket notice indicated that the purpose of the picket was 'to attract public attention to violations of the human right of access to a court'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket organisers misled the officials of the Yekaterinburg town administration as to the real purposes of their action.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that instead of drawing public attention to the problems of judicial protection and violations of human rights as indicated in the picket notice, for three days the picket participants distributed printed leaflets and materials of a slanderous and insulting nature which targeted the president of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court personally.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the information contained in the extract from the Novaya Gazeta newspaper was more than two years old.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the information in the Novaya Gazeta newspaper extract had been checked by the Supreme Qualification Panel of Judges and the Prosecutor General's Office and found to be slanderous.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket participants, in particular Mr Sh. and Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), were perfectly aware that the information in the Novaya Gazeta newspaper extract had been found to be slanderous.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket organisers deliberately and maliciously changed the nature of the action and thereby misled the public.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that the picket organisers committed an administrative offence by violating section 4 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council of 28 July 1988, as amended by the Presidential Decree of 25 May 1992.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev stated that pursuant to section 8 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council of 28 July 1988, Mr Sh., Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), and Ms M. were administratively liable under Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev asked the head of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department of Yekaterinburg to institute administrative proceedings against Mr Sh., Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), and Ms M. in accordance with Article 28.3 § 2 (1) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev asked the head of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department of Yekaterinburg to prepare a report on an administrative offence and decide on the issue of the legal responsibility of Mr Sh., Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), and Ms M. for the breach of law.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his letter of 27 March 2003, Mr Dementyev requested to be informed of the decision taken by the Verkh-Issetskiy police department of Yekaterinburg.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 17 April 2003, an official of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department of Yekaterinburg compiled a report on administrative offences committed by the applicant under Article 20.2 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code on Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the report of 17 April 2003, the applicant had given notice of the picket too late.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the report of 17 April 2003, the applicant had distributed leaflets of a slanderous and insulting nature against the president of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the report of 17 April 2003, the applicant had obstructed the passage of citizens into the court-house of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Court bailiffs Mr R. and Mr M. were listed as eyewitnesses in the report of 17 April 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 21 April 2003, the head of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department forwarded the report on administrative offences and supplementary materials to the Verkh-Issetskiy District Court of Yekaterinburg.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The administrative offence matter was assigned to the justice of the peace of the 3rd Court Circuit of the Verkh-Issetskiy district of Yekaterinburg.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 15 May 2003, the applicant challenged the judicial formation and requested that the matter be examined in a neighbouring region.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant claimed that objective examination of the matter in Yekaterinburg was impossible because it had been initiated at the instigation of high-ranking officials of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace dismissed the applicant's challenge, holding that under the Code on Administrative Offences there were no legal grounds to change the venue.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 19 May 2003, the justice of the peace issued a ruling on an administrative offence (постановление по делу об административном правонарушении) in which she found the applicant guilty on three counts.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace held that the applicant had breached the established procedure for organising a picket by sending the picket notice eight days before the picket date.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace held that both the 1988 USSR Supreme Council's Decree and the local Yekaterinburg regulation on public assemblies established a ten-day notification period for pickets.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace found the applicant guilty of breaching public order during the picket, relying on the report on an administrative offence dated 17 April 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified in court that they worked as court bailiffs in the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that at about 9.10 a.m. on 25 March 2003 they had gone onto the porch of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court and seen some people with banners, among them Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant) holding the banner 'Ovcharuk – resign'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that the picket participants were standing on the porch right in front of the entrance on the top floor, blocking the passage and distributing leaflets.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that when they asked the picket participants to show their identity documents and go down the stairs, the participants refused, but went down after a police officer approached them.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Witnesses Mr M. and Mr R. testified that judges coming to work had told them that the picket participants had blocked access to the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace relied on the report by court bailiff Mr R. of 25 March 2003 as evidence of the applicant's guilt.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace relied on the report by police officer Mr G. from the Verkh-Issetskiy police station, which indicated that between 25 and 28 March 2003 he had been responsible for public order during the picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Police officer Mr G.'s report stated that the picket had been organised by Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), Mr Sh., and Ms M., who at 9 a.m. on the day of the picket were standing on the staircase at the entrance to the Sverdlovsk Regional Court and thus obstructing access to the building.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Police officer Mr G.'s report stated that following his intervention and that of the court bailiffs, the picket participants went down to the pavement in front of the court-house and did not subsequently interfere with the normal functioning of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace did not accept the arguments by the applicant's representative that the applicant did not block access to the Sverdlovsk Regional Court, because those arguments contradicted the evidence already examined in court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace noted that the defence witnesses were present at the picket from 9.30 a.m., by which time the picket participants had already descended the staircase on orders of the police officer and were no longer blocking access.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace held that photographs produced by the defence and examined in court could not prove that the applicant did not block access to the court-house, because they depicted solely the moment when they were taken rather than the entire time during which the picket had been held, and because the court did not know when the photographs were taken.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace found that the picket had been conducted at variance with the aims listed in the notice.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the notice dated 18 March 2003, the initiative group of citizens comprising Mr Sh., Mr Kuznetsov (the applicant), and Ms M. held a protest action against violations of citizens' right to judicial protection.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant's representative explained in court that the picket aimed at attracting public attention to the problems of judicial protection, such as refusals to accept a claim or unfair judgments.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Witness Mr M. stated that he had brought and distributed a newspaper describing certain instances in which citizens' rights to judicial protection had been breached.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The picket participants distributed extracts from the Novaya Gazeta newspaper containing A. Politkovskaya's article 'Ovcharuk and his team', which in its contents did not correspond to the aims of the picket as stated in the notice.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The distribution of the Novaya Gazeta newspaper extracts was not contested by the applicant's representative in court and was also confirmed by witnesses.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace declared the applicant guilty under Article 20.2 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace fined the applicant 1,000 Russian roubles (approximately 35 euros).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 11 July 2003, the Verkh-Issetskiy District Court of Yekaterinburg, on an appeal by the applicant, upheld the ruling of the justice of the peace.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Verkh-Issetskiy District Court of Yekaterinburg endorsed the reasons given by the justice of the peace in upholding the ruling.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The judgment of the Verkh-Issetskiy District Court of Yekaterinburg of 11 July 2003 was final as no further ordinary appeal lay against it.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Russian Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of peaceful assembly and the right to hold meetings, demonstrations, marches and pickets under Article 31.
The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 was in force at the material time pursuant to Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992.

Under section 2 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to give written notice to the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly.

Under section 3 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, the municipal authority was required to give its response no later than five days before the assembly.

Under section 4 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, assemblies were to be conducted in accordance with the aims listed in the notice and with respect for Soviet laws and public order.

Under section 8 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, individuals who breached the established procedure for organising and holding assemblies incurred liability under the laws of the USSR and Soviet republics.

Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code on Administrative Offences provides that a breach of the established procedure for organising a demonstration, meeting, procession or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum monthly wage, which was 1,000 to 2,000 Russian roubles at the material time.

Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code on Administrative Offences stipulates that a breach of the established procedure for holding a demonstration, meeting or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum wage for organisers, or five to ten times the minimum wage for participants.
